best_for: People leaving a browser's built-in password saver who want an open-source manager with email aliases, and a free plan that works on every device.

points.title: Free has no device limit
points.text: Proton Free works on unlimited devices with 2 vaults, 10 hide-my-email aliases and 1 GB of file storage. The built-in 2FA code generator is not part of the free plan.

points.title: What Pass Plus adds
points.text: Pass Plus is USD 1.99 per month on a 12-month plan (USD 23.88 the first year, then USD 35.88). It adds unlimited aliases, 2FA codes, item and vault sharing, dark web monitoring, file attachments, emergency access, a command-line tool and up to 50 vaults. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Family and bundle plans
points.text: Pass Family covers six people for USD 2.79 per month (USD 33.48 the first year, then USD 59.88) with an admin panel. Proton Unlimited adds Mail, Drive, VPN and Calendar for USD 6.49 per month. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Open source and audited
points.text: The apps are GPL-3.0 and Proton says the code is public and reviewed by outside auditors.

points.title: Browser extensions too
points.text: Proton offers extensions for Chrome, Firefox, Brave, Edge and Safari, so the same vault works in the browser as well as in the desktop app.

points.title: Linux: DEB and RPM from Proton
points.text: Proton's Linux guide offers a DEB for Debian and Ubuntu and an RPM for Fedora. The Flatpak listed here is a Flathub build that is not marked verified.

points.title: Windows is an MSIX package
points.text: The Windows app comes as an x64 MSIX that needs Windows 10 version 1903 or later. The Mac app is universal and needs macOS 13. The Windows listing keeps 44 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
